title: 🏛️ America Puts 'Megaspeed' on the Blacklist! The Company at the Heart of a Scandal Smuggling Nvidia Chips to China!
body: 🏛️ America Puts 'Megaspeed' on the Blacklist! The Company at the Heart of a Scandal Smuggling Nvidia Chips to China!

The U.S. Department of Commerce added the Singaporean company Megaspeed and six other companies in Southeast Asia to its Entity List on Monday, a move that effectively bars them from buying advanced AI chips without a U.S. government license.

The department's Bureau of Industry and Security said the seven companies are acting 'in a manner contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States,' and that they were listed because of a significant risk that they are, or may be, involved in diverting advanced computing products to unauthorized users.

The list includes three companies in Malaysia, two in Singapore, and one in Thailand, among them a unit of Alibaba called Apex Enterprise Solutions, which denied any diversion of banned chips. Malaysia also said it would notify data center operators not to deal with the listed companies.

Megaspeed is at the heart of a scandal involving the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China: the U.S. Department of Justice is investigating it, and Washington accuses its former CEO, Alice Huang, of working for Chinese intelligence — accusations Beijing has denied, calling them 'baseless speculation.' Reports said the company has imported Nvidia equipment worth at least $4.6 billion through its subsidiaries since its founding in 2023.

The listing came just hours after Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, after the U.S. President personally intervened with the board, and the company's shares jumped 31.5% on the news of his return — the strongest day for the U.S. market in more than 18 months.
Simply put: Washington bans the middleman while at the same time allowing some chips to be sold to China directly... So do blacklists really stop smuggling, or are they just a political message?
Do you think banning companies is enough to stop the smuggling of advanced chips?
